$comment: ADR-037 register fragment (connectors-hr-data-exchange, Task 1, design D1). The dormant SFTP drop of a payroll bureau without an API: the source and the mapping that renders a humaniq PayrollHandoff's mutations as the rows of one CSV file per period. No code: the synchronization engine and the SFTP adapter do the work.

objects.name: Payroll bureau SFTP drop
objects.description: A payroll bureau that takes its mutations as a file: one CSV per administration and period, named <loonheffingennummer>-<period>.csv, delivered into the bureau's incoming folder; the bureau's return file with the payslips is picked up from its outgoing folder. Set the location, the root path, a brokered credential and the server's host key fingerprint (the first test shows it), agree the folders and the delimiter with the bureau, then enable.

objects.name: humaniq payroll handoff to a bureau CSV file
objects.description: One humaniq PayrollHandoff, read with its PayrollHandoffMutation objects as `mutations` and its administration as `administration`, as one CSV file for the bureau: the file name <loonheffingennummer>-<period>.csv, and one row per changed field with the loonheffingennummer, the period, the humaniq employee id, the mutation kind, the effective date, the field, the old and the new value. A value that is itself a list or an object is written as JSON in its cell. Off until the bureau source is set up; the push that delivers it is payroll-handoff-push (connectors-hr-data-exchange D1).

mapping.rows: {% set rows = [] %}{% for m in mutations|default([]) %}{% for field, change in m.fields|default({}) %}{% set rows = rows|merge([{'loonheffingennummer': administration.loonheffingennummer|default(''), 'periode': period, 'medewerker': m.employeeId, 'soort': m.kind, 'ingangsdatum': m.effectiveDate|default(''), 'veld': field, 'oud': change.old is iterable ? change.old|json_encode : change.old ?? '', 'nieuw': change.new is iterable ? change.new|json_encode : change.new ?? ''}]) %}{% endfor %}{% endfor %}{{ rows|json_encode }}
